# Security measures

<!-- Generated by scripts/export-security-measures.js from src/config/securityPosture.js. Do not edit by hand. -->

IDevelop Community Edition documents **45 security controls** in 5 areas. Each one cites the code that implements it and the automated tests that prove it. The same list is shown in the application under **About → Security**.

A test (`tests/unit/securityPostureEvidence.test.js`) fails if a cited file or test disappears, so this page cannot claim a control the code no longer has.

## Web application protection

| Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Implemented in                                                                                                          | Proven by                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Content Security Policy with a per-request nonce; no inline event handler (onclick…) can run (script-src-attr none); the relaxed policy of the standalone guides applies only to a closed list of documents; Helmet headers, HSTS over HTTPS, clickjacking protection.                                                                                                                                                       | `server.js`<br>`src/utils/tlsServer.js`<br>`public/js/csp-actions.js`<br>`src/middleware/httpHardening.js`              | `tests/unit/webSecurityBaseline.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/noInlineHandlers.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/trustProxyAndStaticCsp.test.js`                                                                                   |
| Security headers: Permissions-Policy (camera, microphone, location, payment, USB, Bluetooth denied), COOP/CORP isolation, no referrer to another site (none at all from the APIs), no framework banner; dynamic pages never cached, browser cache cleared at sign-out; health probes give no detail to an anonymous caller.                                                                                                  | `server.js`<br>`src/middleware/httpHardening.js`                                                                        | `tests/unit/asvsHeaders.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/httpHardening.test.js`                                                                                                                                             |
| JSON APIs (/api/v1, SCIM) refuse any request body that is not JSON (415).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `src/middleware/jsonContentType.js`                                                                                     | `tests/unit/asvsHeaders.test.js`                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Anti-CSRF token on every form and call that changes data, file uploads included (the token travels in a header, or in the address of a plain upload form; no upload is exempt); an origin check on every state-changing request (a "null" origin is refused); bulk approvals also ask for the session token.                                                                                                                 | `server.js`<br>`src/middleware/httpHardening.js`<br>`public/js/main.js`                                                 | `tests/unit/webSecurityBaseline.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/httpHardening.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/csrfMultipart.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/approveAllSessionCsrf.test.js`                                                 |
| Output escaped by default; every raw output and every script that writes HTML is inventoried and reviewed; stored text and every query parameter of every page are proven escaped by tests over the real application.                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `views/partials/json-script.ejs`<br>`src/utils/queryParams.js`                                                          | `tests/unit/c317-C-dom-xss.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/reauditXssSinks.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/rawOutputInventory.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/storedTextEscaped-db.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/queryParamMatrix-db.test.js`    |

| Webhooks and AI providers: internal, loopback and metadata addresses are refused (an on-premises AI model must be allowed by name by a super-administrator); the connection is pinned to the checked address, with no redirect.                                                                                                                                                                                              | `src/services/WebhookService.js`<br>`src/services/CopilotService.js`                                                    | `tests/unit/securityControls.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/copilotPresetsAndEmails.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/copilotEgressGate.test.js`                                                                                    |
| Uploaded files checked on every upload route: the content must match the extension (magic bytes, OOXML content types, macros refused), a file name with a folder path, a control character or more than 200 characters is refused, size and entry count capped (zip-bomb protection), parser errors answered as client errors; cell values escaped on display; an SVG logo is served under a policy that forbids any script. | `src/utils/importGuards.js`<br>`src/utils/fileSignature.js`<br>`src/middleware/uploadGuard.js`<br>`src/routes/index.js` | `tests/unit/securityAudit20260929.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/asvsHeaders.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/uploadFileSignature.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/uploadGuardMounts.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/uploadNameAndAvMounts.test.js` |

| Request size capped and expensive actions rate limited; free-text reasons capped at 2,000 characters on every route; linear regular expressions on untrusted text; the trusted proxy (TRUST_PROXY) validated at start-up, a value that would trust every client is refused.                                                                                                                                                  | `server.js`<br>`src/middleware/rateLimiter.js`<br>`src/utils/validators.js`<br>`src/middleware/httpHardening.js`        | `tests/unit/webSecurityBaseline.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/loginRateLimiterCountsFailures.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/reasonCapUsernameRedos.test.js`<br>`tests/unit/trustProxyAndStaticCsp.test.js`                      |

## Standards and frameworks

The controls are mapped to the standards below. **This is a self-assessment by the development team, not a certification.** OWASP ASVS 4.0.3 level 2 was verified requirement by requirement: 258 requirements, **166 pass** and **19 fixed** during the assessment, 37 partial, 2 open gaps, 29 not applicable and 5 not verifiable from the code (`docs/ASVS-L2.md`). The other frameworks are mapped control by control in `docs/COMPLIANCE-MAPPING.md`, which also lists what the deploying organisation must still do.

| Framework                                | Basis         | Details                      |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------- |
| OWASP ASVS 4.0.3 — Level 2               | self-assessed | `docs/ASVS-L2.md`            |
| OWASP Top 10 (2021)                      | mapped        | `docs/COMPLIANCE-MAPPING.md` |
| CWE Top 25 (2024)                        | mapped        | `docs/COMPLIANCE-MAPPING.md` |
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A               | mapped        | `docs/COMPLIANCE-MAPPING.md` |
| SOC 2 (CC6, CC7, CC8)                    | mapped        | `docs/COMPLIANCE-MAPPING.md` |
| GDPR (Articles 5, 15–17, 25, 30, 32, 35) | mapped        | `docs/COMPLIANCE-MAPPING.md` |
| EU AI Act (Articles 13, 14)              | mapped        | `docs/COMPLIANCE-MAPPING.md` |
| NIST SSDF (SP 800-218)                   | mapped        | `docs/COMPLIANCE-MAPPING.md` |

## Running the security tests

```bash
npm test                                   # the whole suite, as CI runs it
npx jest tests/unit/webSecurityBaseline.test.js tests/unit/securityControls.test.js tests/unit/securityPostureEvidence.test.js
npm audit --omit=dev                       # known vulnerabilities in dependencies
```

## Known limitations

- The CSP still allows inline event handlers (`script-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'`) and inline styles; inline `<script>` blocks need the per-request nonce. Moving the remaining `onclick=` handlers to scripts is planned.
- Without `APP_KEY` or `SESSION_SECRET` (development only), stored secrets are kept in clear; production refuses to start without a strong secret.
- No independent penetration test has been published yet. One is recommended before general availability; see `docs/SECURITY-AUDIT.md` for the internal audit and `SECURITY.md` for reporting a vulnerability.
